complexity.notes: The dict is really an array indexed by 0..n-1 (consecutive int keys, so no hashing risk), and `list(range(n))` around the range is redundant. Representing parent pointers as closures is clever but very hard to read; a plain `parent` list with an explicit find loop would express the same algorithm far more directly. There is also redundant work: `a` and `b` are already roots, so `component[a]()` and `component[b]()` in the comparison just re-resolve the same roots — the test could compare `a != b` directly. The real cost is that unions are ordered by node index only, so chains of linear depth can form and each find walks the whole chain (hence the huge recursion-limit bump, which is the only change from the previous submission and does not affect the algorithm); adding ||union by rank/size together with path compression|| would bring this down to near-linear, effectively O(m α(n)). Note that a very deep recursive resolve is still a stack-depth risk even with the raised limit.
complexity.summary: A union-find where each node's parent pointer is stored as a lambda in a dict, so calling component[x]() recursively resolves x to its component root; each edge that joins two distinct roots decrements the component count, with the smaller-indexed root kept as the parent.
